tasks.short: Design integrated spatial and non-spatial databases for GIS use.

steps.what: Agree GIS use cases, source ownership and integration constraints with users
Design spatial entities, non-spatial tables, keys and database relationships
Validate the schema against sample data, topology rules and query needs
Check and save the final schema and development handoff specification

tasks.design: Use a native schema editor in the GIS tooling category of {OTHER} to represent chosen entities and relationships once. Render its field dictionary into {DOCS}, retaining human design choices, sample-data validation and final review before saving the development handoff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schema diagrams and field dictionaries duplicate the same design decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native schema editors can export diagrams and dictionaries from a single model.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing correct spatial granularity, keys, topology and ownership across sources.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve conflicting user concepts and assess whether a schema supports real spatial questions.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate schema drawing and documentation; the same database design authority.

reach.learn: Spatial indexing and data ownership contracts

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: schema editors can reuse entity definitions to render diagrams and field dictionaries; they do not decide the appropriate data model.

assumptions: Boundary is design and development coordination, not production database deployment. Save approval covers the design artefact only.

Source owners supply source ID, fields, types, coordinate reference system, update frequency and ownership. s2 manually chooses entity, geometry type, key, relationships, nullability and topology constraints. Missing descriptions require manual clarification.
The native editor removes duplicate drawing and dictionary copying only. s2 retains all design judgement; s4 retains final validation and saves the completed export.
Test native {OTHER} schema export first. Existing exports earn no new saving; all shares are provisional.
research_questions: Does the generated dictionary match the final schema including spatial constraints?

incremental.description: Maintain dictionary export fields and schema-editor compatibility

approvals.approved_version: Final schema model and rendered handoff reviewed immediately before saving the same revision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 9%: 8 duplicate-schema hours and 2 dictionary-copying hours removed, less 1 upkeep. Low assumes diagrams are already generated and only negligible handoff work remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with users to analyze, configure and troubleshoot GIS applications.

steps.what: Confer with users to establish the GIS problem and expected result
Reproduce the issue and choose a safe configuration or troubleshooting action
Check and apply the chosen configuration with the user
Draft the support resolution record with the actual settings and outcome
Check and commit the final resolution note to the support case

tasks.design: Configure a {HELPDESK} resolution form that reuses the case, application and user identifiers. Keep the user discussion, reproduction and configuration decision human; the technologist enters actual settings and outcome, then checks and commits the completed case note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Support records repeat identifiers and basic problem headings after the user session.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case forms can reuse case data without generating a diagnosis or asking users to repeat entry.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing data, projection, permission and application faults.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the user is trying to achieve and confirm the fix in that workflow.
tasks.altitude: A modest reduction in support paperwork, unchanged troubleshooting and access authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native case forms can reduce repeated support metadata entry while preserving human troubleshooting.

assumptions: Boundary includes user discussion, configuration and case documentation. Users' session time is existing outside labour and unchanged; no self-service transfer is proposed.

Existing case data supplies case ID, user ID and application version. s2 produces a tested setting change with rollback. In s3 the technologist checks the exact preview before deliberately applying it and confirms outcome with the user.

s4 manually captures changed settings, cause if known and observed outcome; only identifiers and headings prefill. Missing case metadata stays manual. s5 keeps full final semantic check and save time.
First test native {HELPDESK} forms. No baseline is assumed for repeated searching or application runtime; shares are unmeasured.
research_questions: Do forms reduce repeated entry without encouraging unsupported root-cause statements?

incremental.description: Maintain the resolution form and application identifier list

approvals.approved_version: Exact tested configuration preview and target checked immediately before manual application; any changed setting requires review
Final resolution note checked against actual settings and outcome immediately before saving

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 3.1%: 3.6 repeated record-entry hours removed, less 0.5 upkeep. Low assumes most record fields are unique and prefill saves only its upkeep. User discussions and troubleshooting remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect and integrate GIS data for map manuscripts.

steps.what: Choose GIS sources suitable for the map's extent, date and scale
Collect the selected remote sensing or cartographic files and metadata
Integrate GIS layers through approved reprojection, clipping and field mapping
Check spatial alignment, coverage, attributes and licensing of the integrated layers
Commit the approved layers to the map manuscript workspace

tasks.design: Use native batch collection and saved processing recipes in the GIS tooling category of {OTHER}. Reuse the selected source list, extent and target projection while retaining manual source choice, exception handling and complete spatial checks before a gated workspace commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated downloads and per-layer parameter entry are separate manual operations.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch processing can reuse validated mappings across comparable layers.
tasks.still_hard: Different vintages, licenses and spatial accuracies can make technically aligned sources unsuitable.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether the combined map supports its intended use without misleading precision.

ambition.what: Refresh a draft map's source coverage after each new approved imagery release.

tasks.altitude: Less repeated layer setup, more time checking source suitability. Publication rights do not change.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: saved GIS processing recipes can reuse projection, clipping and schema mappings for compatible datasets.

assumptions: Boundary is collection and integration for a map manuscript, not publication. No remote sensing acquisition runtime is counted as human effort.

Catalogue producers supply dataset ID, revision, extent, acquisition date, coordinate reference system, license and download reference. s1 selects sources. Missing metadata keeps collection manual in s2.

The technologist supplies target projection, clipping boundary and field mapping in the approved recipe. s3 remaining time includes manual recipe adaptation and unmatched formats; no automatic schema guessing is assumed.

s4 checks geometry and semantic suitability, not just successful execution. First test native {OTHER} batch collection and processing. Existing automatic transformations earn no new saving; shares cover manual parameter entry and repetitive operations only.
research_questions: What fraction of layers can reuse a recipe without manual projection or attribute repair?

already_counted.description: Final spatial, attribute and licensing check

incremental.description: Maintain source endpoints and processing recipes

approvals.approved_version: Final integrated layer hashes, source versions and manuscript destination checked in s4; changes require reapproval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: fourteen collection and twenty-one repeated-processing setup hours saved less two upkeep. Low: bespoke layers need all manual collection and integration. Workspace commitment, source choice and final checks retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Transfer and rescale photographic information onto maps or other photographs.

steps.what: Choose corresponding control points and check source photograph geometry
Set rescaling and transformation parameters for the photographic transfer
Transfer interpreted photographic features onto the map or target photograph
Verify residual alignment, feature placement and acceptable scale distortion
Save the approved rescaled information in the controlled map workspace

tasks.design: Configure saved transformation presets and batch parameter reuse in the GIS tooling category of {OTHER}. Keep control-point selection, feature interpretation and distortion checks human, and save only the accepted transfer revision; native resampling computation already exists and earns no labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable photographs require repeated transform and export settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presets can reuse target scale, projection and resampling parameters while preserving per-image checks.
tasks.still_hard: Poor control points, relief displacement and ambiguous photographic features.
tasks.human_edge: Know whether visual alignment hides an unacceptable spatial error.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated parameter entry, the same responsibility for cartographic accuracy.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: georeferencing tools can reuse transformation presets; control-point quality and acceptable distortion still require judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is photographic transfer and rescaling, including feature interpretation and saving, not new imagery acquisition.

s1 produces source pixel coordinates, reference map coordinates and point IDs. The map owner supplies target scale, coordinate reference system and resolution; the technologist selects transform family and resampling mode in s2.
Presets apply only to comparable image sets. Missing geometry or excessive residual error requires manual parameters within s2 and full checks in s4; no model infers control points.
Test native {OTHER} presets first. Saving comes from repeated human parameter entry and manual saving, not computation or unchanged feature tracing. Estimates are provisional.
research_questions: Do reused settings preserve acceptable residuals across the actual photograph types?

approvals.approved_version: Final rescaled image and transferred features with target workspace approved in s4; edits invalidate approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: fifteen repeated-parameter hours saved less two upkeep. Low: photographs share no reusable preset and upkeep remains. Same-workspace save, control points and interpretation retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce duplicate GIS configuration and documentation while preserving spatial design and accuracy judgement.
role.ambitious_version: Refresh draft maps from approved sources more often with traceable, human-checked spatial data.

job.title: Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians
